title: Human Resources Officer
experience_raw: Senior (5+ years of experience)
raw_text: TERMS OF REFERENCE (TORs) FOR RECRUITING HUMAN RESOURCE OFFICER FOR FAWE RWANDA CHAPTER 1. Background The Forum for African Women Educationalists (FAWE) is a membership-based Pan-African Non-Governmental Organization that operates through 34 National Chapters in 33 countries in Sub-Saharan Africa to promote girls’ and women’s education. FAWE’s vision, mission and goal focus on quality education for girls and women socio-economic empowerment. FAWE Rwanda is one of 33 national chapters. FAWE Rwanda Chapter was started in 1997 and since its inception, FAWE Rwanda has grown to become a reputable partner and focal point on female education in Rwanda. FAWE Rwanda Chapter would like to recruit a Human Resource Officer for an initial period of three years, renewable based on performance and availability of Funds, with a probationary period of three months. Details of the position are provided below: Position: Human Resources OfficerReports to: Executive Director 2. Job Purpose The core purpose of the Human Resources Officer is to support the Executive Director in the effective management and administration of the organization’s human resources. The position is responsible for supporting staff recruitment and onboarding, maintaining personnel records, coordinating staff performance management and capacity-building initiatives, administering staff welfare and benefits, and ensuring compliance with FAWE Rwanda’s human resources policies, procedures, and applicable employment regulations. The Human Resources Officer will also promote gender-responsive, equitable, and inclusive human resource practices aligned with FAWE Rwanda's mission of advancing girls' and women's education and empowerment, while championing organizational values, staff wellbeing, safeguarding, and professional excellence. 3. Key Responsibilities Serve as the focal point for the Human Resources function within the organization and provide timely HR support to management and staff. Support workforce planning and ensure the effective implementation, interpretation, and continuous improvement of HR policies, procedures, systems, and practices. Support strategic workforce planning, succession planning, and talent management initiatives to ensure the organization attracts, develops, and retains high-performing employees. Coordinate end-to-end recruitment and selection processes, including developing job descriptions, preparing vacancy announcements, shortlisting candidates, coordinating interviews, conducting reference checks, facilitating onboarding, and ensuring timely updates of employee information in the ERP system. Maintain accurate, complete, and confidential employee records, including personnel files, staff databases, employment contracts, leave records, attendance records, and other HR documentation, ensuring that relevant information is properly maintained in the ERP system. Coordinate the staff performance management process in collaboration with Department Heads, including performance planning, objective setting, performance appraisals, feedback, and follow-up on performance improvement and development plans. Support employee engagement and welfare initiatives, address workplace concerns appropriately, and promote a positive, respectful, inclusive, and productive working environment. Coordinate staff wellbeing initiatives and promote a healthy work environment through wellness programs, psychosocial support initiatives, and work-life balance practices. Work with management to identify staff capacity-building and professional development needs and coordinate relevant training, staff orientation, coaching, mentoring, and other learning and development initiatives. Develop and implement annual staff learning and development plans to strengthen organizational capacity and support career growth. Collaborate with the Finance and Administration Department to provide accurate and timely HR information for payroll processing and ensure the effective administration of employee benefits in accordance with organizational policies, with relevant transactions and records maintained through the ERP system. Monitor and administer staff attendance, leave, and other absences, ensuring compliance with approved policies and procedures and maintaining accurate records through the ERP system. Ensure compliance with applicable HR policies, procedures, and employment legislation, including FAWE Rwanda policies and relevant labor laws and regulations in Rwanda. Coordinate the implementation of safeguarding, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA), anti-harassment, and child protection policies, ensuring staff awareness and compliance with organizational standards. Prepare and submit regular HR reports to the Executive Director and provide management with accurate and timely HR information on staffing levels, recruitment, turnover, leave, attendance, performance, training, employee welfare, and other relevant HR matters. Analyse workforce data and HR trends, including staff turnover, recruitment efficiency, retention, training effectiveness, and employee engagement, to support evidence-based management decisions. Facilitate effective HR communication by communicating HR policies, procedures, benefits, and organizational decisions to staff and providing appropriate guidance and clarification on HR-related matters. Coordinate employee lifecycle processes, including induction, probation monitoring, confirmation, promotion, transfer, resignation, termination, exit interviews, clearance, and separation procedures. Provide HR advisory support to management and employees on HR policies, employee relations, performance management, and other employment-related matters, while supporting the fair, consistent, and confidential resolution of workplace issues. Identify and monitor HR-related risks and recommend appropriate mitigation measures to ensure organizational effectiveness and compliance. Ensure confidentiality and proper management of employee data by safeguarding personnel information, maintaining secure HR records, and ensuring that access to confidential employee information is restricted to authorized personnel in accordance with organizational policies and applicable data protection requirements. 4. Reporting and Working Relationships The Human Resources Officer will report to the Executive Director or designated supervisor and will work closely with programme, finance, administration, and other departments to ensure effective human resource management across the organization. 5. Qualifications and Experience A bachelor’s degree in human resources management, Business Administration (Specialization in Human Resource Management), or a related field with at least 5 years of relevant experience in human resources management, preferably within an NGO or similar organization. or A master’s degree in human resources management, Business Administration (Specialization in Human Resource Management), or a related field with at least 2 years of relevant experience in human resources management, preferably within an NGO or similar organization. Professional certification in Human Resources Management is an added advantage. Training or certification in safeguarding, child protection, gender equality, diversity and inclusion, or organizational development will be an added advantage. Good knowledge of employment practices, HR policies, and applicable labor laws in Rwanda. Experience in recruitment, talent management, performance management, employee relations, learning and development, safeguarding compliance, and HR administration. Strong communication, interpersonal, organizational, and problem-solving skills. Good computer skills, including proficiency in Microsoft Office and HR information systems. High level of integrity, confidentiality, professionalism, and attention to detail. 6. Key Competencies The Candidates should have the following key competencies: Human resource management and administration, Recruitment and talent management, Employee relations, Performance management, Training and capacity development, Strategic workforce planning, Leadership and people management, Coaching and mentoring, Organizational development, HR analytics and data-driven decision-making, Gender-responsive human resource management, Diversity, equity and inclusion, Safeguarding and child protection, Change management, Risk management and compliance. Communication and interpersonal skills, Planning and organizational skills, Conflict management and problem-solving, Confidentiality and integrity, Teamwork and collaboration. Commitment to girls' education, women's empowerment, gender equality, and safeguarding principles. 7. Key Deliverables The Human Resources Officer will be expected to deliver: Accurate and up-to-date personnel records and HR databases (ERP-Microsoft Dynamics 365). Timely and well-coordinated recruitment and onboarding processes. Effective implementation of staff performance management processes. Regular HR reports submitted to management. Effective administration of staff leaves, benefits, and welfare. Coordinated staff training and capacity-building activities. Compliance with HR policies and applicable employment regulations. A professional, supportive, and productive working environment. Annual staff learning and development plan implemented. Quarterly HR workforce analytics reports submitted to management. Staff well-being and engagement initiatives effectively coordinated. Safeguarding and PSEA compliance measures implemented and monitored. Updated succession planning and talent management records maintained. Gender-responsive and inclusive HR practices promoted across the organization. 8. Duration and Terms of Employment The appointment will be for an initial period of three years, renewable based on performance and availability of Funds with a probationary period of 3 months) 9. Remuneration and Benefits FAWE Rwanda Chapter offers a competitive remuneration package commensurate with the successful candidate’s qualifications, skills, and relevant professional experience. The benefits package includes medical insurance, pension contributions, maternity leave, airtime allowance, and annual leave, in accordance with FAWE Rwanda’s policies and applicable employment regulations 10. Job application procedures Application letter addressed to FAWE Rwanda National Coordinator and Education certificates (combined in pdf); Recent Curriculum Vitae (CV) with proven work Experience including three referees (combined in pdf). Highly qualified candidates should send their cover letter; well detailed CV and copies of degrees and certificates. How to Apply Interested candidate should submit their application no later than 15th October 2026. Please click on the “Apply” button to complete your application. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Apply

title: Analyst, Office of the CFO (Fixed-term)
experience_raw: Senior (5+ years of experience)
raw_text: About One Acre Fund Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post. About the Role Seeking an exceptional finance professional with experience to strengthen the CFO's office, driving strategic initiatives and turning complex data into decisions that shape Finance operations organisation-wide. Responsibilities Division Communications & Executive Support Lead the drafting and delivery of Finance Division communications, including decision announcements, priority rollouts, and key organisational cycles. Maintain the Division's communications calendar and coordinate inputs, timelines, follow-ups, and actions with department leads. Prepare high-quality presentation decks, briefing notes, data summaries, and other materials for senior leadership. Translate complex data, analytical findings, and team inputs into clear insights, recommendations, and actionable messages. Division Operations & Governance Coordinate the Finance Division's governance calendar, including leadership meetings, quarterly forums, annual events, and other key planning cycles. Support agenda development, meeting logistics, preparation of materials, and follow-up on key decisions and actions. Monitor progress against divisional priorities and OKRs, identifying risks, dependencies, and areas requiring leadership attention. Maintain clear trackers and work plans to support effective coordination and execution across the Division. Strategic Projects & Problem Solving Own clearly defined projects and workstreams from planning through execution and delivery. Coordinate selected CFO- and Senior Manager-sponsored initiatives by aligning stakeholders, tracking milestones, and proactively addressing blockers. Lead or contribute to high-priority cross-functional and ad hoc projects across the Finance Division. Apply structured problem-solving to ambiguous challenges and develop practical options and recommendations for leadership. Analysis, Strategic Insight & Flexible Resourcing Conduct research, benchmarking, data synthesis, and financial analysis to support strategic decision-making. Develop structured outputs, including summaries, frameworks, financial models, and scenario analyses. Provide flexible support across the Finance Division during periods of peak demand, staff transitions, or extended leave. Take ownership of assigned responsibilities during temporary assignments, ensuring clear communication, continuity, and effective handover. Support divisional recruitment and other priority initiatives as needed. Career Growth and Development We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career. Qualifications Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have: Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, or a related field. CPA or ACCA finalist. About 5 years of working experience in finance, strategy, consulting, project management, or operations, within fast-paced medium- to large organisations. Strong stakeholder management and cross-functional collaboration skills. Proactive, detail-oriented, and solutions-focused approach. Familiarity with financial analysis, management reporting, and business decision-making is preferred. Comfortable navigating ambiguity and adapting to changing priorities. Full professional proficiency in English, with strong written communication skills. Preferred Start Date As soon as possible Job Location Kigali, Rwanda Benefits Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits. Contract Duration 2 years, renewable with a high chance based on good performance. Eligibility This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Rwanda. Application Deadline 28 November 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made. One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. Apply

title: Biobank Head
experience_raw: Senior (5+ years of experience)
raw_text: Description Position Title: Biobank Head Department: Institute of Global Health Equity Research (IGHER) Duty Station: UGHE-AVEGA Biobank and UGHE, Kigali. Frequent travel to the Butaro campus, Northern Province, Burera District, Rwanda Contract Duration: Two (2) years, renewable based on performance Position Summary The Biobank Head provides strategic, scientific, technical, and operational leadership for the establishment and management of the UGHE-AVEGA Biobank, a core research infrastructure of the Institute of Global Health Equity Research (IGHER). The position is responsible for leading the planning, establishment, operationalization, accreditation, and continuous improvement of the biobank to support clinical trials, translational research, precision medicine, genomics, oncology, infectious diseases, non-communicable diseases, and population health research. The Head is responsible for the overall administration and day-to-day management of biobank operations, including biospecimen acquisition, processing, storage, inventory management, retrieval, distribution, Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) administration, quality management systems, biosafety and biosecurity, regulatory compliance, equipment management, financial oversight, and supervision of biobank personnel. Reporting to the Clinical research lead/Director of IGHER, the Biobank Head works closely with the Head of the UGHE-AVEGA Clinical Trial Unit to ensure seamless integration of biobanking services into all clinical trials and research activities conducted through UGHE. The position also collaborates closely with the Biobank Project Consultant (External Scientific Consultant) to establish the biobank according to international standards, develop governance structures, implement quality systems, strengthen institutional capacity, and position UGHE as a national and regional centre of excellence in biobanking. The Biobank Head will play a pivotal leadership role in developing institutional policies, standard operating procedures, governance frameworks, regulatory systems, quality assurance programs, and strategic partnerships that ensure the biobank operates in accordance with ISBER Best Practices, ISO 20387, Good Clinical Laboratory Practice (GCLP), Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and all applicable national and international regulatory requirements. Key Responsibilities Lead the establishment and operation of the UGHE–AVEGA Biobank and align activities with UGHE/IGHER priorities. Establish SOPs, Quality Management Systems, governance, and regulatory compliance, including preparation for ISO 20387 accreditation and ISBER Best Practices. Lead implementation and management of the LIMS and ensure secure, accurate, and traceable data management. Oversee biospecimen management, quality, traceability, security, staffing, equipment, budgets, and daily operations. Integrate biobanking with clinical trials and research programs and develop national and international collaborations. Build staff capacity through training, mentorship, and competency development in biobanking, GCP/GCLP, biosafety, and quality management. Qualifications Education PhD (preferred) or Master's in Biobanking, Medical Laboratory Sciences, Biomedical/Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Pathology, Genomics, Public Health, Clinical Research, or related field. Certification in GCLP, GCP, ISO 20387, ISO 15189, ISBER Best Practices, or QMS/Laboratory Management is a plus. Experience 8+ years in biobank management, biomedical research, clinical laboratory management, or clinical trial support, including 5+ years in senior leadership supervising multidisciplinary teams Proven track record establishing or expanding a biobank/biospecimen repository — infrastructure planning, workflow development, and operations Experience implementing LIMS and laboratory/biobank Quality Management Systems Hands-on management of biospecimen collection, processing, cryopreservation, storage, and distribution Equipment lifecycle management (procurement through calibration/maintenance) Experience managing donor-funded programs, budgets, and strategic/donor reporting Developed SOPs, quality manuals, and governance structures (Oversight/Scientific Advisory/Data Access Committees) Prepared labs for ISO 20387, ISO 15189, or ISBER accreditation; built CAPA and audit systems Prepared IRB/ethics/regulatory documentation; ensured compliance with biospecimen collection, storage, and export regulations Developed informed consent, data privacy, and biobank governance frameworks Supported regulatory inspections and audits Strong command of ISBER, ISO 20387/15189, GCLP/GCP, LIMS, and biosafety/QMS standards. Excellent leadership, project and financial management, and scientific writing/communication skills. Experience establishing a national/regional biobank; integrating biobanking into clinical trials; working with international institutions or in LMIC/Africa settings; PMP/PRINCE2 certification; strong publication and grant-management record. To apply Applicants should provide: (1) a curriculum vitae, (2) graduate transcripts, (3) examples of relevant teaching experience or course materials, where available, and (4) a personal statement describing their teaching approach and experience working with diverse student populations. Applicants may also include an example of relevant scholarly work. Please upload these under the ‘Additional Files’ tab on the application page. University of Global Health Equity is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Organizational Profile UGHE is a new kind of university focused on training the next generation of global leaders in health care delivery. The university launched in Rwanda in September 2015. Through an academic experience uniquely rooted in the values of equity, students are empowered to both ease suffering at the bedside and drive transformational, systemic changes to the health system. UGHE is an initiative of Partners In Health (PIH), an internationally recognized non-profit organization whose mission is to provide a preferential option for the poor in health care. In over nearly three decades of operating alongside public sectors in countries around the world, PIH has developed a model to deliver high quality healthcare to some of the world’s most marginalized communities. Nowhere has this impact been more profound than in Rwanda, where Inshuti Mu Buzima-PIH’s sister organization and our government partners have driven innovation for a decade. Members of the UGHE community are tenacious and resolute in our drive to attain social justice, make common cause with those in need, listen to and learn from others, and operate with honesty and humility as we uphold academic integrity and intellectual curiosity. The University of Global Health Equity seeks individuals committed to these values to join the team. Commitment to Safeguarding and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Sexual Harassment: At UGHE, we are committed to ensuring that those who benefit from our work- including community members – as well as our students, contractors, staff, and visitors to our campus are treated with dignity and respect and protected from sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment and any form of systemic abuse, whilst reducing risk and vulnerabilities. A range of pre-employment checks will be undertaken in conformity with UGHE’s policy. UGHE will request information from applicants’ previous employers about any findings of fraud, harassment, sexual harassment and any form of systemic abuse or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By applying, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures. Apply

title: Assistant Teacher Trainer - Inclusive Education
experience_raw: Entry level (1 to 3 years of experience)
raw_text: JOB OPPORTUNITY Assistant teacher trainer-Inclusive Education Location: Kigali-Rwanda Contract:One year renewable ABOUT THE MOYO CENTER The Moyo Center is a Rwanda-based organization working to strengthen inclusive education through teacher training, professional development, research, curriculum development, and community building. Our goal is to help create educational environments where children with disabilities, including children with autism and other learning and developmental differences, can meaningfully learn, participate, and thrive. THE OPPORTUNITY We are looking for an enthusiastic, practical, and growth-minded Assistant Teacher Trainer – Inclusive Education to join our team. The successful candidate will work closely with our Senior Teacher Trainers to co-facilitate professional development, assist in school coaching, support demonstration classrooms, and help design practical learning materials for partner schools. This role is ideal for an educator with strong classroom experience or early experience in teacher support who is eager to build their skills in adult training, coaching, and inclusive curriculum development. PURPOSE OF THE ROLE The Assistant Teacher Trainer will support the planning and delivery of training programs that equip teachers with the skills to support learners with diverse needs. The role involves co-facilitating workshops, assisting with classroom observations and follow-ups, supporting resource creation, and contributing to a continuous learning model across partner schools. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 1. Training Assistance & Co-Facilitation Assist in preparing and co-delivering interactive, practical training sessions for teachers and school staff. Help set up and facilitate workshops, small group discussions, hands-on activities, and classroom simulations. Support the gathering of participant feedback and assist in adapting materials to meet teacher needs. 2. Inclusive Education Practice & Support Support teachers in implementing foundational inclusive strategies, including differentiated instruction, positive behavior support, classroom accommodations, and communication tools. Support strategies tailored for learners with autism, learning disabilities, and other developmental differences. 3. Coaching, Observation & Follow-Up Conduct follow-up visits to partner schools to observe classroom practice under the guidance of senior trainers. Provide constructive, encouragement-focused feedback to teachers. Help model effective inclusive techniques alongside classroom teachers. Assist in tracking teacher progress and identifying common classroom challenges. 4. Materials & Content Development Assist in drafting and organizing training presentations, handouts, visual aids, and low-cost classroom learning materials. Support the contextualization of inclusive education tools for the Rwandan school context. 5. Demonstration Classrooms & Documentation Assist in setting up and maintaining model inclusive classrooms. Help document success stories, lessons learned, and training data for monitoring, evaluation, and learning (MEL) purposes. 6. Stakeholder Engagement Maintain positive, respectful relationships with teachers, school administrators, and families during school visits and training events. QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE Required Rwandan nationality. Bachelor’s degree or Diploma in Education, Special Needs Education, Inclusive Education, Psychology, or a related field At least 1 to 3 years of direct teaching experience or early experience assisting in teacher training/coaching. Basic understanding of child-centered learning and inclusive education principles. Good facilitation, presentation, and interpersonal skills. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. Professional fluency in written and spoken English. Fluency in Kinyarwanda. Strongly Preferred Direct experience teaching or supporting learners with autism, intellectual disabilities, or special educational needs. Experience creating practical teaching aids or learning materials. Familiarity with Rwandan public school contexts and basic inclusive education guidelines. HOW TO APPLY Please submit the following documents to olivier@aeprogram.org: Updated CV / Resumé Cover letter detailing your experience and interest in inclusive education Contact details for two professional referees Email Subject: Application – Assistant Teacher Trainer – Inclusive EducationDeadline: 26th October, 2026 Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. The Moyo Center is committed to inclusion, equal opportunity, safeguarding, and creating a safe and respectful environment for all children, educators, and staff. Apply

About Vumbuzi Impact Africa (VIA) Foundation VIA Foundation is a recently founded financial intermediary organization dedicated to supporting the acceleration and scale-up of ecosystem restoration efforts across member countries of the African Forest Landscape Restoration Initiative (AFR100). The mission of VIA Foundation is to provide innovative financial solutions and strategic support to restoration champions, the local organizations that mobilize communities to restore degraded land. As a trusted and up-and-coming intermediary, VIA Foundation intends to mobilize resources, foster partnerships, and drive the implementation of sustainable landscape restoration projects. Its goal is to enhance ecosystem resilience, empower local communities, and contribute to global climate goals. With its growing team and partnerships with leading institutions, VIA Foundation aims to create a legacy of restored landscapes that thrive both ecologically and economically, ensuring a sustainable future for generations to come. VIA Foundation is a partner of TerraFund, a financing consortium that currently funds, trains, and monitors 200+ restoration projects across Africa. TerraFund focuses on deploying grants, low-interest loans, and equity finance to organizations in three key landscapes: the Lake Kivu & Rusizi River Basin (in Burundi, DRC, and Rwanda), the Greater Rift Valley of Kenya, and the Ghana Cocoa Belt. These portfolios are managed through the World Resources Institute’s TerraMatch platform, an end-to-end system that hosts open calls for proposals, connects champions with technical assistance, and tracks the progress of funded projects through a standard monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) protocol. With this data, VIA Foundation is building new partnerships that catalyze finance for restoration outcomes. Internship Highlight: VIA Foundation seeks a Communications Intern to help tell the story of locally led restoration across Africa. Working from the Kigali office, you will help build the foundation’s young public voice producing content for its website and LinkedIn, capturing stories from the restoration champions it finances, and assembling the communications materials that support its partnerships and fundraising. This is a hands-on learning role designed for a recent university graduate who writes well, is curious about restoration and climate finance, and wants to build a professional portfolio. You will be expected to draft, design, publish materials, and take ownership of the pieces assigned to you. You will report to the Grants & Finance Specialist and work closely with VIA Foundation’s Project Managers, its Field Coordinators in Rwanda, Kenya, and Ghana, and communications colleagues at VIA Foundation’s technical partner WRI Africa. Over six months, you will see how an emerging pan-African institution positions itself with funders, governments, and the communities restoring degraded land. Build simple visual assets — social graphics, slide templates, one-pagers, and carousels — using Canva or similar tools, in line with VIA Foundation’s brand guidelines. Maintain an organized library of photos, videos, logos, consent forms, and approved messaging so that materials can be reused quickly and correctly. Support the drafting of communications products that strengthen fundraising and donor engagement, such as impact snapshots, portfolio highlights, and annual report sections. Support the preparation of materials for external forums where VIA Foundation is represented. Digital Channel Management (50%) Maintain and update content on via-foundation.org, including news items, partner pages, and vacancy postings. Prepare, schedule, and publish posts across VIA Foundation’s LinkedIn and monitor comments and messages for follow-up. Build a mailing list of VIA Foundation’s partners through which to share news and updates. Maintain the communications calendar, tracking upcoming publications, events, campaign moments, and portfolio milestones. Compile monthly analytics on website traffic and social media performance, and flag what is working and what is not. Excellent written English, with a demonstrated ability to turn complex or technical material into clear, engaging copy. A portfolio, writing samples, or links to published work are required. Familiarity with major social media platforms and how organizations use them, including basic content planning and audience engagement. Working knowledge of design and editing tools such as Canva, Adobe Creative Suite, or CapCut; comfort with photography or short-form video is an advantage. Basic experience with website content management, e.g., Drupal, and with social media or web analytics is an advantage. Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage several assignments against deadlines in a small, fast-moving team. Demonstrated interest in ecosystem restoration, climate, agriculture, or sustainable development. Comfort receiving and acting on editorial feedback across multiple rounds of revision. Languages: You will be proficient in written and spoken English and fluent in Kinyarwanda. Additional fluency in French and/or Swahili is an asset. Requirements: You must have an existing right to work in Rwanda and be able to work in person from VIA Foundation’s Kigali office. A 1-page cover letter specifying why you are an excellent fit for the internship. Two short writing samples, or links to a portfolio of communications work (published articles, social campaigns, videos, or design pieces). Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. title: Executive Coordinator, ACE-AJ Secretariat
experience_raw: Senior (5+ years of experience)
raw_text: TERMS OF REFERENCE EXECUTIVE COORDINATOR - ACE-AJ SECRETARIAT Position Executive Coordinator, ACE-AJ Secretariat Host institution Legal Aid Forum (LAF), Rwanda Scope Pan-African / multi-country Reporting ACE-AJ Founding Members, through the governance and hosting arrangements of ACE-AJ and LAF Duty station Kigali,Rwanda,withregularregionaland international engagement Contract Full-time; terms to be specified in the employment contract 1. Institutional Background and Rationale The African Centre of Excellence for Access to Justice (ACE-AJ) is a Pan-African platform established to strengthen access to justice, legal empowerment, human rights and people-centred justice across Africa. Its origins lie in a continentally grounded feasibility process undertaken in 2016 through consultations with access-to-justice organisations in Kenya, Sierra Leone, Rwanda, Malawi and South Africa. The feasibility work examined the relevance, scope, sustainability, institutional form and operational requirements of a continental centre and identified the need for a stronger African voice, systematic knowledge exchange, research, learning, capacity development and collaboration among organisations working closest to communities. The feasibility process envisaged the Centre as more than a conventional project or secretariat. It was conceived as a galvanising space for access-to-justice and legal-empowerment actors; a repository of African practice and evidence; a platform for peer learning and exchange; a mechanism for strengthening community-based justice; and a vehicle through which African organisations could develop collective positions and speak with greater coherence on continental and global justice questions. ACE-AJ was officially launched in Kigali, Rwanda, in 2017. Since its establishment, it has evolved into a multi-country network bringing together civil society organisations and justice actors committed to expanding access to justice for poor, vulnerable and marginalised communities. The Legal Aid Forum (LAF), Rwanda, is a founding member and hosts the ACE-AJ Secretariat. ACE-AJ’s Strategic Framework 2024–2030 provides the current institutional roadmap. It organises the Centre’s work around five mutually reinforcing priorities: promoting holistic justice delivery; strengthening capacity building; research and knowledge generation; advocacy and communication; and strengthening the ACE-AJ Secretariat. The Strategy also places substantial emphasis on monitoring, learning, institutional visibility, membership growth, strategic partnerships and diversified resource mobilisation. 2. Purpose and Strategic Character of the Position The Executive Coordinator is the principal executive and operational lead of the ACE-AJ Secretariat. The purpose of the position is to provide disciplined continental coordination and executive leadership for the implementation of ACE-AJ’s Constitution, Strategic Framework 2024–2030, decisions of the General Assembly and Board, approved programmes and institutional commitments. The Executive Coordinator will move ACE-AJ from strategy to implementation. The office holder will connect a geographically dispersed membership, translate strategic priorities into annual and multi-year plans, mobilise resources, coordinate multi-country programmes, strengthen governance and institutional systems, generate and communicate evidence, develop strategic partnerships and position ACE-AJ as a credible African platform on access to justice, legal empowerment and people-centred justice. The position therefore requires a network builder and institutional entrepreneur, not only a programme administrator. The Executive Coordinator must combine continental vision with implementation discipline; diplomacy with accountability; strong member relations with external representation; and programme leadership with fundraising, knowledge generation and organisational development. 3. Overall Accountability Serve as the principal executive focal point for implementation of ACE-AJ’s Strategic Framework 2024–2030 and approved annual priorities. Ensure that decisions of the General Assembly and Board are translated into clear workstreams, responsibilities, timelines, budgets, deliverables and measurable results. Lead the day-to-day work of the Secretariat and coordinate Secretariat personnel, consultants, technical advisers and designated support from member organisations. Maintain effective operational coordination with LAF as host institution while safeguarding ACE-AJ’s distinct continental identity, governance and member ownership. Provide timely, evidence-based advice to the Board on institutional development, programme performance, partnerships, funding, risks and emerging access-to-justice trends. 4. Key Responsibilities 4.1 Continental Network Coordination, Membership and Movement Building Provide proactive day-to-day coordination of ACE-AJ as a Pan-African network and maintain substantive engagement with members across countries, regions, legal traditions and languages. Develop an annual member-engagement architecture covering consultations, focal-person meetings, peer exchanges, communities of practice, thematic working groups, institutional visits and regional or continental convenings. Maintain structured two-way communication between the Secretariat, Board, General Assembly, founding members, and strategic partners. Map and continuously update member expertise, innovations, community-justice models, research, policy experience, institutional capacities and support needs. Strengthen member ownership by creating practical opportunities for members to lead research, training, advocacy, convening and cross-country initiatives. Lead strategic membership growth, with particular attention to geographic balance and stronger representation from underrepresented parts of the continent. Coordinate membership admission, onboarding, orientation, retention and an accurate, functional membership database. Identify common challenges across jurisdictions and convert them into collective learning, research, advocacy and programme initiatives. 4.2 Strategy Implementation and Institutional Performance Translate the 2024–2030 Strategic Framework into costed annual work plans, implementation matrices, institutional calendars and measurable performance commitments. Coordinate implementation across all five strategic priorities and ensure that programme choices remain connected to ACE-AJ’s mission, comparative advantage and member experience. Develop a Secretariat performance dashboard showing progress against strategic outcomes, programme commitments, membership engagement, partnerships, fundraising, visibility and governance decisions. Institute quarterly implementation reviews and prepare concise performance briefs for the Board. Identify implementation bottlenecks, emerging risks and opportunities and recommend corrective measures. Coordinate periodic strategy reviews and contribute evidence for the development of ACE-AJ’s post-2030 strategic direction. 4.3 Holistic and People-Centred Justice Advance ACE-AJ’s agenda on holistic justice delivery by connecting formal, informal and community-based justice actors and approaches. Promote recognition of community-based justice practitioners and strengthen their contribution to accessible, affordable and responsive justice systems. Support member initiatives that demonstrate how legal empowerment, mediation, community justice, legal aid and other people-centred approaches can complement formal justice institutions. Facilitate cross-country learning on enabling policy and regulatory environments for community-based justice and paralegal practice. Ensure that the perspectives of poor, vulnerable and marginalised communities remain central to ACE-AJ’s programmes, research, advocacy and institutional narrative. 4.4 Capacity Building and Peer Learning Develop and coordinate a continental capacity-building programme informed by member needs and the Strategy. Organise practical peer-to-peer learning, mentorship, technical exchanges and cross-country exposure among members. Develop partnerships with universities, legal aid clinics, professional bodies, judiciaries and specialist institutions for training, research and professional development. Promote learning models that draw systematically on the experience of ACE-AJ members rather than relying exclusively on external expertise. Support development of scalable training resources and, where feasible, longer and more intensive learning programmes for community-based justice practitioners. 4.5 Research, Evidence and Knowledge Management Lead implementation of ACE-AJ’s research and knowledge-generation agenda, including practitioner-driven and comparative research with continental policy relevance. Coordinate documentation of best practices, innovations, impact case studies and lessons from member organisations. Develop and maintain an accessible knowledge-sharing platform or e-repository for research, laws, policies, tools, case studies and member resources. Promote common or compatible data-collection approaches across members to strengthen the African evidence base on access to justice. Coordinate research partnerships with universities, research institutions and practitioners and ensure appropriate ethical, data-protection and quality standards. Translate research into policy briefs, position papers, learning products, advocacy messages and practical tools for members and decision-makers. 4.6 Continental Advocacy, Policy Influence and Representation Develop and coordinate ACE-AJ’s continental advocacy agenda, drawing on member evidence and experience. Support development of coherent African positions on legal empowerment, community justice, legal aid, people-centred justice and related emerging issues. Build structured engagement with the African Union, African Commission on Human and Peoples’ Rights, regional economic communities, United Nations mechanisms and other relevant regional and global institutions. Identify opportunities for ACE-AJ and its members to contribute to justice-sector reform, policy processes, legislative discussions and international forums. Represent ACE-AJ at authorised regional, continental and international engagements and prepare high-quality briefs, statements and speaking points. Ensure that ACE-AJ’s advocacy elevates member expertise and community experience rather than substituting for them. 4.7 Strategic Communication, Visibility and African Narrative Lead implementation of an institutional communication and visibility plan that establishes ACE-AJ as a recognised source of African expertise on access to justice and legal empowerment. Oversee regular member updates, newsletters, website content, social media, publications and other institutional communication. Develop a compelling evidence-based continental narrative demonstrating ACE-AJ’s added value and the contribution of its members. Increase dissemination and citation of ACE-AJ research, policy products and member-generated knowledge. Coordinate media engagement and ensure consistent branding, messaging and recognition of member organisations. 4.8 Resource Mobilisation and Financial Sustainability Develop, maintain and drive a diversified resource-mobilisation strategy and funding pipeline aligned with ACE-AJ’s strategic priorities. Map foundations, bilateral and multilateral partners, international organisations, corporate and philanthropic actors and other potential supporters. Lead or coordinate high-quality concept notes, proposals, budgets, partnership submissions and donor presentations. Build and maintain long-term donor and strategic-partner relationships and coordinate due diligence, negotiations, stewardship and reporting. Explore sustainable non-grant income approaches consistent with ACE-AJ’s mandate, governance and applicable legal requirements. Work with the host institution and relevant governance structures to ensure sound grant management, financial controls, compliance and transparent reporting. Strengthen ACE-AJ’s ability to demonstrate impact as a central element of fundraising and partnership development. 4.9 Programme Development, Multi-country Implementation and Accountability Design and coordinate multi-country and network-wide initiatives from concept development through implementation, monitoring, learning and reporting. Develop clear implementation arrangements with participating members, including roles, deliverables, budgets, timelines, reporting requirements and decision-making arrangements. Track delivery across countries and intervene early where implementation is delayed or quality is at risk. Coordinate narrative and management reporting to the Board, members, partners and donors. Ensure programmes demonstrate clear value to participating members and contribute to ACE-AJ’s strategic outcomes rather than operating as isolated projects. 4.10 Governance and Institutional Development Provide high-quality technical and administrative support to the Board and General Assembly. Coordinate AGMs, Board meetings and other governance processes, including agendas, briefing papers, minutes, decision registers and systematic follow-up. Maintain constitutional, governance, membership, programme and institutional records. Support development, review and implementation of policies, manuals, procedures and internal systems required for a credible continental institution. Ensure Secretariat operations comply with the ACE-AJ Constitution, approved policies, governance decisions and relevant legal and contractual obligations. Support the establishment and effective operation of thematic working groups, committees, patrons or other mechanisms provided for in ACE-AJ’s strategic and governance framework. 5. Expected Results and Performance Indicators ACE-AJ functions as an active, connected and member-owned continental network with demonstrably regular and substantive member participation. Annual strategic priorities and governance decisions are implemented, tracked and reported systematically. Membership expands strategically and becomes more geographically and linguistically representative. Regional and continental exchanges, working groups and joint initiatives produce documented learning and collaborative action. ACE-AJ generates and disseminates credible African evidence, research, best practices and policy products. ACE-AJ’s visibility and participation in relevant African and international justice platforms increases. A credible and diversified funding pipeline is maintained, with stronger donor stewardship and institutional sustainability. Multi-country programmes demonstrate timely delivery, accountability, learning and clear value to participating members. Governance, programme, financial, membership, partnership and communication records are accurate, current and accessible. ACE-AJ increasingly contributes an identifiable African voice to debates and policy processes on access to justice, legal empowerment and people-centred justice. 6. Qualifications and Experience Master’s degree in law, Human Rights, Development Studies, Public Policy, International Relations, Governance, Programme Management or a closely related field. A strong bachelor’s degree combined with substantial relevant senior experience may be considered. At least 5 years of progressively responsible professional experience in access to justice, legal empowerment, human rights, governance, civil society strengthening, international development, network leadership or a closely related field. Demonstrated experience coordinating a network, coalition, secretariat, regional platform or multi-country partnership. Substantial experience working across several African countries is strongly preferred. Demonstrated ability to translate strategy into implementation plans, budgets, partnerships, programmes and measurable results. Strong experience in programme design and management, monitoring and learning, budgeting, reporting and institutional planning. Proven experience in resource mobilisation, proposal development and donor or strategic-partner relationship management. Experience supporting governance bodies and organisational/institutional development. Experience in research, policy engagement, advocacy, knowledge management or capacity development relevant to access to justice is highly desirable. Excellent written and spoken English. Working knowledge of French is a strong advantage; knowledge of other widely used African languages is an asset. 7. Core Competencies and Leadership Profile Continental network leadership and movement building. Strategic execution and disciplined follow-through. Member engagement, coalition management and cross-cultural diplomacy. Resource mobilisation, partnership development and donor stewardship. Programme leadership and multi-country coordination. Governance, institutional development and accountability. Research literacy, evidence use and knowledge translation. High-level writing, communication, advocacy and representation. Sound judgement, political and institutional sensitivity, integrity and independence. Ability to work effectively across borders, time zones, institutions and professional cultures with limited supervision. 8. Particular Profile Sought ACE-AJ is seeking an Executive Coordinator who can build an institution and a continental network at the same time. The successful candidate will be comfortable engaging organisational leaders, practitioners, community-justice actors, academics, donors, governments, regional institutions and international partners. The person must be able to create trust among members while maintaining delivery discipline and accountability. Candidates should demonstrate through concrete examples how they have coordinated networks or multi-country partnerships; converted strategy into implementation; maintained active member participation; handled competing institutional interests; mobilised resources; built strategic partnerships; convened diverse actors; generated or used evidence for policy influence; and contributed to institutional growth, visibility and sustainability. 9. Reporting, Supervision and Working Relationships The Executive Coordinator shall report to the ACE-AJ Founding Members in accordance with the Constitution and shall operate within the agreed hosting arrangements with LAF. The Executive Coordinator will work closely with the Chairperson and other Board members, the General Assembly, member organisations and designated focal persons. For hosted administrative functions, the Executive Coordinator will maintain close operational coordination with the Executive Director and relevant departments of LAF. The Executive Coordinator will supervise ACE-AJ Secretariat personnel and coordinate consultants, technical advisers, interns, service providers and staff designated by member organisations to support ACE-AJ activities, subject to approved structures and budgets. 10. Eligibility and Right to Work in Rwanda This recruitment is primarily intended for Rwandan nationals and non-Rwandan nationals who are already legally resident in Rwanda and authorised to work in Rwanda. Due to the resources available for this position, ACE-AJ/LAF will not provide international relocation, expatriate benefits, or sponsorship for relocation to Rwanda. Applicants must therefore be able to take up the position in Kigali under an existing lawful right to reside and work in Rwanda. 11. Application Requirements Applicants should submit a curriculum vitae, a letter of motivation, copies of relevant degree(s) and certificate(s), and two professional references. The motivation letter should specifically demonstrate experience in coordinating networks, coalitions or multi-country partnerships and provide concrete examples of continental or cross-country coordination, strategy implementation, convening, membership engagement, partnership development and resource mobilisation. Applications should be addressed to the Executive Director of LAF, as host of the ACE-AJ Secretariat, and submitted by email to legalaidrwanda@gmail.com with a copy (cc) to ace.a2j@gmail.com The deadline for submission of applications is 30 October 2026. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Apply

raw_text: Tour Guide Driver Company: Sambora Private Journeys Location: Rwanda — based in Kigali, with travel nationwide Employment: Full-time About Sambora Private Journeys Sambora Private Journeys is the private touring and safari arm of Sambora, crafting tailor-made journeys across Rwanda — from Kigali and Volcanoes National Park to Nyungwe, Lake Kivu and Akagera. The Role This is much more than a driving role. Our Tour Guide Drivers are the face of Sambora Private Journeys throughout a guest's time in Rwanda. We are looking for exceptional guides who combine safe, professional driving with genuine warmth, outstanding knowledge of Rwanda and the ability to turn an itinerary into a memorable private journey. You will accompany guests from arrival to departure, taking responsibility for the smooth day-to-day delivery of their journey. You will be expected to understand your guests, anticipate their needs, adapt your style to different travellers and provide knowledgeable, engaging interpretation of Rwanda's history, culture, wildlife, conservation and landscapes. The best guides know when to share a story, when to start a conversation and when to simply allow guests to enjoy the journey and their surroundings. Key Responsibilities 1. Guest Experience & Journey Delivery Welcome guests warmly and professionally at airports, hotels, lodges and other meeting points, assisting with luggage and ensuring an excellent first impression. Provide safe, comfortable and punctual transportation for airport transfers, day tours and multi-day journeys throughout Rwanda. Adapt professionally to weather, road conditions, delays or changing guest needs, communicating proactively with the operations team before making significant itinerary changes. Identify guest concerns early and work calmly and professionally with the operations team to resolve them. 2. Guiding & Interpretation Provide engaging, accurate and thoughtful interpretation of Rwanda's history, culture, communities, conservation, wildlife, birdlife and landscapes. Conduct Kigali and other city tours, cultural visits, scenic journeys and game drives to a consistently high standard. Spot, identify and interpret wildlife and birdlife while ensuring respectful and responsible wildlife viewing. Brief guests thoroughly before activities such as gorilla and chimpanzee trekking, including what to expect, park regulations and what to bring. Continually develop your knowledge of Rwanda, its destinations, history, wildlife, conservation and contemporary life. Adapt your guiding and communication style to different guests, recognising when guests want conversation and interpretation and when they prefer privacy or quiet. Promote responsible tourism by respecting communities, wildlife, national parks and the environment and encouraging guests to do the same. 3. Guest Care & Professional Conduct Build warm but professional relationships with guests while maintaining appropriate boundaries and discretion. Respond to questions, requests and concerns calmly, confidently and professionally. Maintain complete guest confidentiality and respect the privacy of every traveller. Never photograph, film or post guests, their movements or their itineraries publicly without appropriate permission. Understand journey inclusions and arrangements and avoid discussing confidential company rates, commissions or commercial agreements with guests or suppliers. Maintain an excellent standard of personal presentation and represent Sambora professionally at all times. 4. Follow Rwandan traffic laws, national park regulations and Sambora's safety procedures at all times. Maintain defensive driving practices on highways, urban roads, gravel roads, mountain routes and off-road park tracks. Plan routes carefully and allow sufficient time for traffic, weather, road conditions, park or border checkpoints and scheduled activities. Maintain accurate trip, mileage, fuel or charging, vehicle and expense records and submit them on time. Manage park documentation, permits, vouchers and other tour documentation as assigned. Maintain receipts and supporting documentation for company expenditure. Complete trip reports following journeys, including relevant guest feedback, incidents, operational observations and suggestions for improvement. Use WhatsApp, navigation applications and Sambora's digital systems confidently for operational communication and reporting. Support other touring and operational responsibilities when reasonably required. Minimum three years' relevant experience as a tour guide driver, safari guide or in a comparable tourism role. Valid Rwandan driving licence appropriate for the vehicles operated. Proven experience driving 4x4 vehicles and confidence on rough, gravel and off-road terrain. Excellent spoken English and Kinyarwanda, with the confidence and vocabulary to engage naturally with international guests. French, German or another international language is a strong advantage. Excellent knowledge of Rwanda's national parks, destinations, road network, history, culture, wildlife and tourism experiences. Comfortable using smartphones, digital navigation, WhatsApp and electronic reporting systems. The Person We're Looking For Qualifications and experience matter, but so does personality. You should be: A natural host who genuinely enjoys looking after people. An engaging storyteller with curiosity and a desire to keep learning. Warm and personable without being intrusive. Able to read guests and adapt your approach to different personalities, cultures and expectations. Calm and resourceful when plans change or problems arise. Safety-conscious and disciplined behind the wheel. Reliable, punctual and highly organised. Discreet and respectful of guest privacy. Proud to represent Rwanda and passionate about sharing the country with visitors. Comfortable working flexible hours and spending extended periods away from Kigali, including weekends and public holidays. Training and opportunities to continue developing your guiding, destination and professional skills. The opportunity to join a growing Rwandan hospitality and private travel company committed to delivering exceptional experiences and showcasing Rwanda at its very best. raw_text: CHAI RWANDA VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT Title: Associate, Data Scientist Program: Health Systems Strengthening Job Location: Kigali, Rwanda Type: Full-Time Paid Start date: Immediate Overview The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems. CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic, with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work in conjunction with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally. At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work: http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture. Programs Overview The Government of Rwanda (GoR) strives to achieve Universal Health Coverage (UHC) by enabling equitable access to quality health services for the population as outlined in the Fourth Health Sector Strategic Plan (HSSP IV). This commitment has been made against a backdrop of rising health care costs and uncertainty around the future availability of donor funding and calls for improved health sector sustainability. Acknowledging this, the Government aims to employ effective, equitable, efficient, and sustainable health care financing and systems strengthening, putting an emphasis on primary health care as the cornerstone of a strong and sustainable health system. CHAI Rwanda’s Health System Strengthening (HSS) programs work on a day-to-day basis with Government leadership in the Ministry of Health (MoH) and the Rwanda Social Security Board (RSSB). The goal of those programs is to support the Government to accelerate progress towards UHC by ensuring the sustainable delivery of quality, essential health services. This includes designing and implementing national Primary Health Care (PHC) reforms from health center level down to community health, to increase health workforce availability, to prioritize and sustainably finance essential services, and to support improved management, financing, and delivery of quality primary health care. Position overview CHAI currently seeks an Associate Data Scientist to work with the Ministry of Health (MOH), reporting directly to the head of data science at the National Health Intelligence Center to help improve the quality, governance, and use of evidence on policy decision making. S/He also reports in parallel to CHAI, HSS digital health program manager for specific CHAI supported initiatives. The role ensures that health data is transformed into high-quality, reliable, explainable, and decision-ready intelligence that informs AI development, policy decisions, and health system performance improvement. This role serves as the technical bridge between raw health data, AI models, and real-world decision-making, ensuring scientific rigor, reproducibility, and national-scale usability. Health Systems Intelligence & Decision Support Develop decision-support analytics and public health dashboards for disease burden tracking, resource allocation and service delivery optimization. BACKGROUND AND JUSTIFICATION Association Rwandaise des Conseillers en Traumatisme (ARCT-RUHUKA) is a national non-governmental organisation of professional trauma counsellors established in 1998. ARCT-RUHUKA was subsequently formally established and obtained legal recognition as a non-governmental organisation under Ministerial Decree No. 97/11 of 28 July 2007. The organization was later legally registered with the Rwanda Governance Board (RGB) under Legal Personality No. 97/11 dated 12 September 2013. In accordance with the applicable legal and regulatory framework, ARCT-RUHUKA has continued to maintain its legal compliance and institutional standing. Its most recent certificate, issued by the Rwanda Governance Board on 30 September 2026, certifies that Association Rwandaise des Conseillers en Traumatisme (ARCT-RUHUKA), a national non-governmental organization with Legal Personality No. 97/11 of 12 September 2013, complies with Law No. 058/2024 of 20 June 2024 and the related regulations. Through its qualified and committed staff, the organisation works across various sectors and communities in Rwanda, providing technical expertise, professional support, and integrated services that promote mental well-being, strengthen resilience, protect vulnerable populations, and improve the overall well-being of individuals, families, and communities To strengthen its governance, operational efficiency, institutional sustainability, and impact on target populations, ARCT-RUHUKA seeks to recruit a qualified and experienced Executive Director with strong leadership, strategic management, program coordination, resource mobilization, and organizational development skills. Identify operational challenges and implement appropriate corrective measures; Ensure business continuity and take immediate action in emergencies within delegated authority, in collaboration with the Board of Directors. 3.3. Over the next five years, Kivu Choice aims to scale into Africa’s largest and most sustainable protein producer, producing and distributing 30,000 tons of fish annually for the Rwandan market and for export across the region. Job Purpose: The Plant Operator leads the day-to-day running of Kivu Choice’s fish processing plant, ensuring that machinery-heavy production lines run safely, efficiently, and without unplanned stoppages. The role owns process control, preventive and corrective maintenance, and quality and food safety compliance across the plant, while leading shift teams and operators. As Kivu Choice scales volumes toward 30,000 tons a year, this position is critical to protecting throughput, yield, and product quality from intake through to cold storage and dispatch. Key Responsibilities: 1. Production & Process Control Plan and run daily production to meet volume, yield, and quality targets across all processing lines. Set, monitor, and adjust process parameters (line speeds, temperatures, and processing times) to keep output consistent. Develop and enforce standard operating procedures (SOPs) for every line and piece of equipment. Identify bottlenecks and lead continuous improvement to raise throughput and reduce waste. Coordinate with harvest, logistics, and sales teams so that raw material intake matches plant capacity and orders. 2. Preventive & Corrective Maintenance Build and run a preventive maintenance schedule for all plant machinery, refrigeration, and utilities. Lead fast troubleshooting and corrective repairs to keep unplanned downtime to a minimum. Maintain equipment history, maintenance logs, and a critical spare parts inventory. Manage external technicians and suppliers for specialized servicing and repairs. Advise on equipment upgrades, new installations, and capacity expansion. 3. Monitor critical control points and ensure corrective action is taken and documented when limits are breached. Enforce hygiene, sanitation, and cleaning-in-place standards across the plant. Prepare the plant for internal, customer, and regulatory audits (e.g. Rwanda FDA, RSB) and close out findings. Ensure full product traceability from raw material intake to finished goods. 4. Cold Chain & Product Integrity Oversee chilling, freezing, and cold storage operations to keep product within required temperature ranges. Monitor and record temperatures across processing, storage, and loading points. Work with logistics to protect cold chain integrity through dispatch and distribution. 5. Shift Leadership & People Management Lead, schedule, and supervise shift supervisors, machine operators, and line workers. Train operators on safe equipment use, SOPs, hygiene, and food safety practices. Set clear performance expectations, give regular feedback, and contribute to performance reviews. Enforce occupational health and safety standards and lead incident investigations. 6. Production Reporting & KPIs Track and report daily, weekly, and monthly KPIs, including throughput, downtime, yield, and waste. Analyze performance trends and present root causes and action plans to management. Maintain accurate production, maintenance, and quality records. Support budgeting for plant operations, maintenance, and spare parts. At least 5 years of experience in a processing plant (food, beverage, dairy, meat, poultry, or fish processing preferred), including hands-on supervision of machinery-heavy production lines. Strong process control skills and proven experience running preventive and corrective maintenance programs. Working knowledge of quality control and food safety standards such as HACCP, GMP, or ISO 22000. Cold chain or perishable-product experience is a strong plus. Monitor fidelity to implementation of study interventions, including MMS, calcium supplementation, IV iron administration, PPH management bundles, and POCUS. Identify gaps in clinical documentation, case management processes, and quality-of-care indicators, and support facilities through mentorship and on-site coaching. Support training and continuous professional development of healthcare providers on study interventions and data reporting requirements. Facilitate learning sessions, case reviews, and feedback meetings to promote knowledge sharing and continuous quality improvement. Ensure timely documentation and reporting of adverse events, protocol deviations, and study-related incidents in line with research and ethical requirements. Collaborate with data managers and the Research Coordinator to ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency of clinical data. Serve as the focal point of communication between field sites and the central project coordination team, ensuring effective follow-up and problem resolution. Contribute to the analysis and interpretation of maternal and neonatal health data to inform implementation improvements. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Medicine and Surgery, Nursing, Midwifery, Public Health, or a related field. A Master’s degree in Medicine, Public Health, Epidemiology, or a related field is an added advantage. Valid professional license to practice in Rwanda is an added advantage. Proven experience in maternal health projects, research, or clinical program implementation. Strong familiarity with Rwanda’s health system, Ministry of Health structures, and national data reporting mechanisms. Demonstrated experience mentoring and supporting healthcare providers in data quality, clinical documentation, and protocol adherence. Experience coordinating field-based health sector activities. Skills & Competencies Strong clinical knowledge in maternal, neonatal, and child health care. Proficiency in Electronic Medical Records (EMR) systems and digital data collection tools. Excellent analytical, organizational, and documentation skills with high attention to detail. Effective communication, facilitation, and interpersonal skills to engage multidisciplinary teams. Strong commitment to ethical research practices, patient confidentiality, and professional integrity. Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and travel frequently to field sites. Why Join This Project? Contribute directly to improving the quality of maternal and neonatal health services in Rwanda. Play a key role in strengthening clinical practice and implementation research at facility level. Work closely with national health authorities and multidisciplinary teams on high-impact interventions. Support evidence-based improvements that influence national health policy and practice. The program seeks to bridge the gap between academia, the workplace, and policy analysis, while equipping young economists with a strong understanding of the role of public policy in sustainably improving the well-being of the population. The program is implemented by MINECOFIN and BNR with the support of GIZ Rwanda. Notably, approximately 90% of staff in MINECOFIN’s Office of the Chief Economist are graduates of the previous eight cohorts. The program is now preparing for its ninth cohort. The YEP combines practical experience with structured learning and mentorship. Participants gain hands-on experience at MINECOFIN and BNR, benefit from mentorship and seminars delivered by national and international experts, complete relevant online and in-person courses, and prepare and present analytical briefs. Their professional conduct and performance are assessed throughout the program. The program targets highly qualified Rwandan economists aged 30 years or below who hold at least a bachelor’s degree in Economics, Development Economics, Macro-Fiscal Economics, International Trade/Economics, Monetary Economics, Econometrics, Statistics, or a related field. A master’s degree in one of these fields is considered an asset. The program combines three main components: (a) a continuous internship with on-the-job training and mentoring; (b) intermittent formal group training in applied economics, quantitative methods, and relevant software/s; and (c) continuous self-study, including a research project at a later stage of the program. The project’s ultimate goal is to generate real-time molecular data to guide policy and programmatic decisions that will sustain Rwanda’s malaria elimination trajectory and contribute to regional and global efforts against antimalarial drug resistance. Therefore, in order to implement the Malaria Molecular Surveillance Project, SFH Rwanda is recruiting a Digital Content Creator. Job summary The Digital Content Creator will support the MMS Project through the development of high-quality digital and visual communication materials aimed at increasing malaria awareness, community engagement, and public understanding of malaria prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and surveillance activities. The position holder will be seconded to work at the RBC, Kigali, with occasional travel to project implementation sites as required.
